proposition: The image of Ibn Turka and Yazdī as failed Sufis, promulgated by Jāmī and his circle, persisted into the 11th/17th century: the Safavid-era Sullam al-Samāvāt tells that they gave up their books to follow a Baghdad master, experienced no mystical opening, left him for Egypt, missed a secluded dervish there, and were told in Tabriz by a majzūba that the Egyptian refused them for their faithlessness.

mediation.who: Abū l-Qāsim Anṣārī Kāzirūnī, Sullam al-Samāvāt (fl. early 11th/17th c.)
mediation.note: MK: Kāzirūnī's source was likely Afżal al-Dīn b. Ḥabīb Allāh Turka (d. 991/1583), his teacher; a moralising tale
